assets.assets/ocean-room-1977.png: Use case: historical-scene. Create a portrait 2:3 architectural presentation painting for a serious international futures conference magazine printed in Tenerife in 1977. A complete, beautifully resolved speculative scene: a small submerged ocean observatory near the volcanic Tenerife coast seen in an architectural cutaway perspective through the water. Upper fifth: pale sky, a believable distant Teide volcanic cone behind rugged layered coast, Atlantic sea horizon. Lower four fifths: deep muted blue-green water; an illuminated modest cylindrical communal underwater room with a faceted glazed dome, steel framing, a couple of tiny seated people visible at a table; a short enclosed tunnel joins a small submarine passenger tram dock at the lower right, pipes and structural supports visibly connect habitat to basalt seabed. Important: believable modest human scale, sea life only underwater, bottom is dark basalt and sparse seaweed, NOT tropical reef. Mature precise 1970s architectural gouache on board, sharp ruling-pen construction lines, broad confident painted planes and shadows, restrained amber interior light against petrol blue. An ambitious proposal presented earnestly. Not cute, not cartoon, not digital CGI, not a sepia washed sketch, not steampunk. Composition fills the frame as a plate, detailed focus low-centre with room around it. No typography, letters, captions, borders, magazine mockup, or distressed paper. Flat scan of original artwork. High resolution suitable for full page print.
assets.assets/hillside-section-1977.png: Use case: historical-scene. A wide landscape 3:2 architectural sectional-perspective drawing made for an experimental 1977 housing conference in Tenerife. Render an inhabited stepped communal settlement on steep volcanic terrain, entirely as an ambitious architect's ruled black ink drawing with sparse flat brick-red and ochre screenprinted color, on clean warm ivory paper. Precise large architectural section cuts from upper left down to lower right through three terraces of simple white masonry homes embedded in dark basalt slope; cut walls heavy black poché, thin ruled interior details, shared shaded kitchen, children in a shaded passage, tiny ordinary human figures, one person repairing a chair, garden plots, cistern, stairs winding with contour, small solar hot-water collectors on flat roofs. Tiny outline of Teide far beyond the hillside. Outer parts become loose contour lines, fine pencil scaffolding and unfilled drawing paper. Different scale details can be suggested in lower margin but no labels and no letters. Confident draughtsmanship reminiscent of a competition presentation board, axonometric section rather than picturesque scene, visibly manually ruled lines, generous paper around edges. It should describe how buildings meet the hillside and how neighbours meet each other. No tall skyscrapers, no arches and domes everywhere, no huge futuristic megastructure, no glossy render, no cute cartoon, no uniform sepia wash, no photorealism, no text. High-resolution architectural linework for printing as a large magazine plate.
assets.assets/glider-station-1977.png: Use case: historical-scene. Portrait 2:3 illustration for an ambitious 1977 European futures conference magazine, an aviation poster plate with no lettering. Tenerife's future personal glider lift station: foreground left is a very tall slender concrete and steel open elevator tower, viewed from the top departure deck looking out and down across a steep volcanic coastal town to dark blue Atlantic, Teide rising inland in distant right background. The large external lift cradle is clearly visible inside the tower, mechanically carrying a small light glider UP to the high launch gallery; a man in ordinary 1970s work clothes attends the cradle. One tiny elegant single-seat fixed-wing glider with slim long wings, no rotor, no engine jet, is banking away from this high platform, gliding DOWN towards a lower receiving court and a second intermediate lift tower in middle distance. A sense of great height and a quietly extravagant human transport scheme. Dramatic strong diagonal perspective, precise hand-drafted industrial architecture, steel rails and exposed cable wheels, small ordinary people. Flat silkscreen colour separations in deep Prussian blue, vermilion orange, black and offwhite, manual airbrush gradients only in sky, hard graphic shadows, fine ink hatch detail. NOT soft watercolour, NOT sepia, NOT cartoon, NOT glossy CGI or modern drone art. More like a bold 1970s illustrated engineering journal advertisement. Keep craft plausibly light, no giant passenger jets. No text, no logos, no captions, no decorative border. High resolution for full-page print.
